This sounds genuinely stressful—having your professional relationships strained over something you've deliberately kept private is a real blow, and it makes sense you're weighing whether to stay or go.

A few things might help clarify the decision. Consider whether the hostility is affecting your ability to do good clinical work, your sense of safety, and your day-to-day wellbeing—not just whether it's uncomfortable. Your instinct that it may ease after the election is reasonable, but "waiting it out" only works if the current situation is tolerable in the meantime. It might also be worth a candid conversation with practice leadership about the professional expectations around treating colleagues respectfully regardless of politics, since that behavior from coworkers isn't really acceptable.

There's no single right answer here—both staying and relocating can be valid. You might give yourself a timeline (say, reassess after the election) with clear markers for what would make you leave sooner. Talking it through with a trusted colleague or your own supervisor/consultant could help too.
